title: Objects and failure in Java
summary: Handle a parse failure explicitly and reason about collections and checked exceptions.

scenario.briefing: An order import reads counts from a text file. Invalid text should produce a safe result instead of crashing the import.

objectives.description: Apply the taught syntax in a working file.
Diagnose a realistic mistake and choose the correct repair.

hints: The parsing call can throw NumberFormatException.
Wrap the parse in a try block.

misconceptions.feedback: Catch NumberFormatException so programming errors are not silently converted into -1.

misconceptions.description: Assuming parseInt returns -1 on bad input.
misconceptions.feedback: parseInt throws. The -1 value exists only because the catch block chooses it.

sections.title: Java functions and collections
sections.body: Methods declare return types and parameter types: static int add(int a, int b) { return a + b; }. List<Integer> values = new ArrayList<>(); grows dynamically. Generics keep element types explicit, and executors run independent work on reusable threads.

sections.title: Java errors and tools
sections.body: Checked exceptions must be declared or caught. A try/catch block around Integer.parseInt can turn invalid text into a clear result. javac compiles, java runs, Maven and Gradle manage builds, and JUnit runs tests.

vocabulary.definition: A named block of behavior with declared parameter and return types.
A collection whose element type is checked by the compiler.
An exception the compiler requires the caller to handle or declare.

Invalid text is handled by the specific parse exception.

steps.title: Find the off-by-one
steps.prompt: The total loop reads past the end of the array. Select the faulty instruction and the correct repair.

fixes.label: Change the condition to index < values.length.
Keep the condition and subtract one from the index inside the body.

steps.explanation: Valid array indexes run from 0 through length - 1. The <= condition reads index length, which is outside the array.

steps.title: Collections and failure

statements.label: A List<Integer> rejects a String element at compile time.
A checked exception must be caught or declared by the method.
Catching every exception is always better than catching the specific one.
Integer.parseInt returns a sentinel value instead of throwing on invalid text.

steps.explanation: Generics preserve element types, and checked exceptions force an explicit recovery decision. Catch the narrowest exception that you can handle.
